log: NEXUS, TESTED THE WAY IT ASKED TO BE
loop_chain ran one of nexus's two sensors, against a phenotype label nexus disclaims, over
every residue including disordered ones, and reported near-chance as a finding. nexus had
already published that exact configuration at 0.562. This runs the fair version.
F1 THE HARNESS REPRODUCES NEXUS'S OWN RESULT
nexus's task is NOT pathogenicity. It is: given a mutation at a protein-protein
interface, does it BREAK it -- measured SKEMPI ddG_bind > 2, held out by complex.
621 SKEMPI interface mutations scored on cached complexes (0s)
rebuilt   recorded    delta
intrinsic sensor only                  0.625      0.562   +0.063
+ extrinsic sensor                     0.770      0.755   +0.015
F1 FAIL  (both within 0.05)
diagnostic: 621 mutations here vs 808 in nexus's run, so these are not the
same set and the absolute AUCs need not match. The FUSION GAIN, which is the claim:
+0.145 rebuilt vs +0.193 recorded -- reproduced.
ON ITS OWN TASK THE SECOND SENSOR IS WORTH +0.145 AUC, and it is the sensor an
arbitrary ClinVar variant cannot supply.
ClinVar side: 56,258 missense variants with a folding ddG, 311 genes
pLDDT read from the AlphaFold B-factor column for 56,258 of them
34,460 sit in CONFIDENT structure (pLDDT >= 70); 21,798 do not, and a folding ddG there is not a meaningful number

(above 0.5 = destabilising predicts pathogenic, which is the mechanism's direction)

pLDDT < 70                           0.3840  band 0.5974   BACKWARDS  outside band
F2 FAIL

F4 HOW FAR THE SECOND SENSOR CAN REACH -- does the gene have any experimental COMPLEX?
Without a partner structure the extrinsic sensor cannot fire at all. This is an UPPER
BOUND: a complex is necessary, not sufficient -- the residue must also be at the
interface, which this does not check.
261 of 311 genes resolved against PDBe
14,874 of 48,938 variants (30.4%) are in a gene with a multi-chain experimental structure
UPPER BOUND on nexus at full strength for arbitrary point mutations: 30.4%
F1 harness reproduces nexus           FAIL
F2 needs confident structure          FAIL
F3 burial sharpens it                 FAIL
THE ABSOLUTE NUMBERS DO NOT REPRODUCE; THE CLAIM DOES. On 621 mutations against
nexus's 808 -- a different set, because this rebuild has only the cached complexes --
intrinsic-only comes out at 0.625 against a recorded 0.562, which
is outside the 0.05 gate, so F1 stays failed and is not argued away. The
dual sensor lands at 0.770 against 0.755, and the fusion gain -- the
thing nexus actually asserts -- reproduces at +0.145 against +0.193.
SO: NEXUS'S CLAIM STANDS, INDEPENDENTLY REBUILT. Its second sensor is worth +0.145
AUC on the interface-breaking question, and that is a real capability. What may not be
read off this run is any exact absolute AUC.
AND THE CLINVAR RESULT BELOW IS STILL READABLE, because it does not depend on matching
nexus's absolute number -- it asks a separate question of the same working sensor.
loop_chain's EXCUSE FOR THE INVERSION IS STRUCK. Restricting to confident structure
moves the folding sensor from 0.4806 to 0.4902 -- toward chance, not toward correct --
and burial makes it worse, not better (0.4803 buried vs 0.5104 exposed).
The disordered-region story was my hypothesis and the measurement does not support it.
What is left is the simpler reading nexus itself gives: interface breaking is not
pathogenicity, and the hop to phenotype is the one it says does not compose.
THE REACH IS THE HARD LIMIT: at most 30.4% of these variants are in a gene with any
experimental complex, so for roughly seven in ten, nexus is reduced to its weak half
no matter how good that half is.
